'''David Herbert Samuel, 3rd Viscount Samuel''' [[Order of the British Empire|OBE]] ({{langx|he|דוד הרברט סמואל}}; 8 July 1922 – 7 October 2014<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.com/2014-10-16/ty-article/.premium/obituary-first-israeli-member-of-the-house-of-lords/0000017f-eadf-d3be-ad7f-faffe2a90000|title = David Samuel, First Israeli Member of the House of Lords, 1922–2014|newspaper = Haaretz}}</ref>) was an [[United Kingdom|Anglo]]-[[Israel]]i chemist and neurobiologist.

Samuel was the son of [[Edwin Samuel, 2nd Viscount Samuel]], and the grandson of the [[British Jews|British-Jewish]] diplomat [[Herbert Samuel, 1st Viscount Samuel]]. He was a second cousin of [[Rosalind Franklin]]. He was educated at [[Balliol College, Oxford]], and served in the [[Royal Artillery]] in the [[Second World War]] in India, Burma and Sumatra, reaching the rank of captain. He then commenced a distinguished academic career, and was one of the founding fathers of the faculty of chemistry at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]. Late in his career, his scientific interests moved from [[physical chemistry]] (particularly [[chemical kinetics]]) to [[neurobiology]]. He was the author of over 300 publications as well as the book ''Memory: How We Use It, Lose It and Can Improve It''.<ref>[http://www.nyupress.org/product_info.php?cPath=49&products_id=1926 www.nyupress.org] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050404171905/http://www.nyupress.org/product_info.php?cPath=49&products_id=1926 |date=2005-04-04 }}</ref>

From 14 November 1978 until 11 November 1999 he was a member of the British [[House of Lords]], although his only appearance in the official record, ''[[Hansard]]'', was taking his oath in 1995.<ref>{{Hansard-contribs | mr-david-samuel | the Viscount Samuel }}</ref> This made him the only Israeli who ever served in this capacity.
